bugLogs.title: Promo banner text has insufficient contrast ratio of 1.46:1
steps_to_reproduce: Locate the promotional banner with the text 'Free shipping on orders over $50 this week only'
Inspect the computed styles of the div.promo element
Calculate the contrast ratio between the foreground color #d9c27a and background color #ffe9a8
bugLogs.expected_behavior: The text in the promotional banner must have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against its background color to meet WCAG 2.1 AA requirements for normal-sized text.
bugLogs.actual_behavior: The text has a contrast ratio of only 1.46:1 (foreground #d9c27a on background #ffe9a8), which is significantly below the required 4.5:1 threshold, making it difficult to read.
bugLogs.suggested_fix: In the CSS rule for div, change color from #d9c27a to #756942 (4.53:1 on #ffe9a8; measured 1.46:1, required 4.5:1).

bugLogs.title: Missing lang attribute on html element
steps_to_reproduce: Open the page c:\Users\sharvari.warudkar\a11y-auto-triage\fixtures\holdout\home.html in a browser
Inspect the <html> element in the DOM
Verify that the lang attribute is present and set to a valid BCP 47 language code
bugLogs.expected_behavior: The <html> element should have a lang attribute with a valid BCP 47 language code (e.g., lang="en") so assistive technologies can determine the default human language of the page.
bugLogs.actual_behavior: The <html> element does not have a lang attribute, preventing assistive technologies from determining the page language.
bugLogs.suggested_fix: Add the lang attribute to the <html> element. Change <html> to <html lang="en"> (or the appropriate language code for the page content).

bugLogs.title: Missing alt text on hero image
steps_to_reproduce: Locate the hero image with src='hero-summer-sale.jpg'
Inspect the element to verify the presence of an alt attribute
Observe that the alt attribute is missing
bugLogs.expected_behavior: The image should have a descriptive alt attribute that conveys the purpose of the summer sale promotion, or role='none' if it is purely decorative.
bugLogs.actual_behavior: The image element has no alt attribute, aria-label, aria-labelledby, title, or role='none'/'presentation', causing screen readers to either announce the filename or skip the content entirely without context.
bugLogs.suggested_fix: Add alt='Summer Sale: Up to 50% off selected items' to img[src='hero-summer-sale.jpg'] to provide a text alternative describing the promotional content.

bugLogs.title: Cart icon link lacks accessible name
steps_to_reproduce: Focus the cart icon link using a keyboard or screen reader
Listen to the announced name of the link
bugLogs.expected_behavior: The link should have a discernible accessible name that describes its purpose, such as 'View cart'.
bugLogs.actual_behavior: The link has no visible text, no aria-label, no aria-labelledby, and no title attribute, resulting in an empty or generic announcement.
bugLogs.suggested_fix: Add aria-label='View cart' to the a.icon-link element

bugLogs.title: Email input lacks persistent label, relies on placeholder only
steps_to_reproduce: Locate the newsletter email input field with id 'news-email'
Observe that the only text associated with the field is the placeholder 'Your email address'
Focus the input field and observe that the placeholder text disappears
Attempt to use a screen reader to identify the purpose of the field
bugLogs.expected_behavior: The email input field should have a persistent, visible label that remains visible when the field is focused and filled. Screen readers should announce a clear, descriptive name for the field.
bugLogs.actual_behavior: The input field only has a placeholder attribute ('Your email address') with no associated <label>, aria-label, aria-labelledby, or title. The placeholder disappears on focus, leaving no visible indication of the field's purpose. Screen readers may announce the placeholder but it is not a reliable or persistent label.
bugLogs.suggested_fix: Add a visible <label> element associated with the input: <label for="news-email">Email address</label> placed before or above the input. Optionally, keep the placeholder as a format hint (e.g., placeholder="you@example.com") but do not rely on it as the primary label.
